title: 45-Day Identification Strategy
name: 45-Day Identification Strategy
metaDescription: Running the 45-day identification window as a fixed submittal deadline for Jacksonville replacement property candidates.

sections.html: The 45-day identification window opens on the day the relinquished property closes and does not pause for weekends, holidays, or a slow lender. Every candidate the exchanger intends to purchase, or count as a backup, has to be named in writing to the qualified intermediary before that window closes. We run it as a fixed submittal deadline rather than a rough target, because there is no extension available once day 45 passes.

sections.heading: Compressing a Jacksonville Search Into Six and a Half Weeks
sections.html:
Forty-five days is short for identifying real property in a metro as spread out as Jacksonville, where a candidate near JAXPORT and the Northside rail corridor can be forty minutes from a beaches-area retail parcel and even farther from land near I-95 and I-10 on the Westside. We start the search before the relinquished property even closes whenever the sale timeline allows it, so the clock is running against a shortlist that already has property tours and preliminary financials attached rather than a blank sheet of candidates.

A compressed search schedule means the qualified intermediary should have a draft identification notice in hand by roughly day 35, leaving a full week and a half to finalize legal descriptions, confirm ownership vesting, and route the document for signature before the deadline.

sections.heading: The Identification Notice Submittal Package
sections.html:
• Legal description or unambiguous street address for each identified candidate
  • Confirmation of which identification rule applies to the list, three-property or 200-percent
  • Signed and dated notice delivered to the qualified intermediary directly, not only routed through the exchanger's broker
  • Proof of delivery, whether by hand, courier, or certified mail
  • A copy retained by the exchanger separate from the intermediary's file

sections.heading: Where Jacksonville Timelines Get Squeezed
sections.html:
The most common squeeze point is a candidate near the Southbank or downtown where an older parcel's legal description needs to be pulled from a plat or survey that takes longer to retrieve than a straightforward suburban address. Military relocation timing tied to Naval Station Mayport or NAS Jacksonville can also shift a tenant-in-place property's availability late in the window, which forces a last-minute substitution on the identification list rather than a calm final review.

A less obvious squeeze point is an out-of-state exchanger unfamiliar with how spread out Jacksonville actually is; a candidate near the beaches and a candidate on the Westside can be forty-five minutes apart in traffic, which limits how many properties can realistically be toured and priced within the same week. We plan the physical tour schedule around that distance rather than assuming every candidate can be seen back to back on a single trip.

sections.heading: Deciding Between Naming Fewer Strong Candidates or More Backups
sections.html:
Some Jacksonville exchangers prefer a short, high-conviction list of two or three candidates they have already toured and priced. Others want the full flexibility of the 200-percent rule to keep five or six options open in case a preferred property falls through in underwriting. Neither approach is automatically better; it depends on how far along diligence already is by day 45 and how much appetite the exchanger has for carrying multiple parallel negotiations at once.

We walk each exchanger through both scenarios explicitly rather than defaulting to one approach, since a shorter list is easier to manage but carries more risk if the single frontrunner falls through, while a longer list demands more parallel diligence work in a window that is already tight.

sections.heading: Confirming Delivery Before the Deadline Closes
sections.html:
An identification notice that is drafted but not actually delivered to the qualified intermediary before midnight on day 45 does not count, regardless of how far along the paperwork was. We confirm receipt in writing rather than assuming an email or fax went through, and we build the final submittal a few days ahead of the deadline so a delivery problem still leaves room to correct it before the window closes for good.

We also keep a secondary delivery method ready as a backup, such as a courier drop confirmed by signature, in case the primary electronic delivery method fails without warning on the day the notice needs to go out. That redundancy has mattered on more than one Jacksonville exchange where an email delivery bounced silently and was not noticed until the following morning, well inside the window but close enough to cause real concern.

faqs.q: Can a Jacksonville exchanger add a property to the identification list after day 45?
faqs.a: No, the list is locked once the 45-day window closes, which is why we recommend finalizing candidates with a buffer of at least a few days rather than filing on the deadline itself.

faqs.q: Does the 45-day window start when the sale contract is signed or when it closes?
faqs.a: It starts on the closing date of the relinquished property, not the contract date, so pre-closing negotiations do not count against the window.

faqs.q: Can an exchanger identify a property they already own?
faqs.a: Generally no, the identified replacement property must be a new acquisition and cannot already be owned by the exchanger at the time of identification.

faqs.q: What if no suitable Jacksonville candidate can be identified in time?
faqs.a: If nothing is validly identified before day 45, the exchange fails and the relinquished-property proceeds become taxable, which is why we start the search before the relinquished sale even closes whenever possible.

faqs.q: Does identifying a DST allocation take less time than identifying direct real estate?
faqs.a: It can, since a DST sponsor typically has offering documents and property information already assembled, which shortens the diligence needed before the identification deadline compared with a direct property search.
